messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@innovex.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-01T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Confidentiality and Marketing Asset Release — NDA Exception Request

Samir,

Thanks for the heads up on the marketing brief. We're ready to move forward but Legal flagged two items in the Order Form/MSA that could block the logo/quote usage: (1) the broad confidentiality carveout in section 7 and (2) the blanket "no public statements" language in the Order Form.

Can you confirm Innovex's ask scope? Specifically:
- Logo use (static logo in case study, website, press kit)?
- Customer quote (short excerpt from the product team interview)?
- Press release mention + embargo timing?

I've attached the Order Form with our inline redlines (see Innovex_OrderForm_v2_redlines.pdf). For Legal: Kimberly / Marissa, please advise whether we can grant a limited marketing exception (approval by Innovex within 5 business days and a 48-72 hour pre-release review) and propose redline language. Samir, copying your Legal team on follow-up.

Thanks,

Sofia Ivanova
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Innovex Legal <legal@innovex.com>
Date: 2028-07-01T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Confidentiality and Marketing Asset Release — NDA Exception Request

On Jul 1, 2028, at 08:12, Sofia Ivanova wrote:
> Samir,
>
> Thanks for the heads up on the marketing brief...

Team — I reviewed the redlines attached by Sofia. High level: we can accommodate a narrow, written marketing exception but we should limit it and add guardrails to avoid leaking sensitive product roadmap or metrics. Suggested approach:

1) Create a "Marketing Reference Exception" clause in the Order Form that only permits:
   - Use of Innovex's logo and short customer quotes (<= 60 words) in marketing materials (case studies, website, press releases) after written approval from Innovex's designated approver.
   - No disclosure of pricing, usage metrics, or roadmap details.

2) Approval cadence: Innovex must provide written comments within 3 business days of receipt of the draft marketing asset; failure to respond will be deemed approval. If Innovex requests edits, Redwood will provide a revised draft within 2 business days.

3) Embargo / press release: Redwood will not publish a press release mentioning Innovex until the final approved asset is received and an embargo date is confirmed in writing.

Proposed redline snippet (to insert near section 7):

"Notwithstanding any confidentiality provisions, Customer grants Redwood a limited license to use Customer's name and logo and a short customer quote for marketing purposes, subject to Customer's prior written approval, which shall not be unreasonably withheld and shall be provided within three (3) business days of submission."

I'm attaching a short draft redline and a one-page exception box that Legal Ops can fold into the Order Form. If Innovex insists on longer approval windows or broader rights, we'll need a commercial concession (e.g., extended pilot credits or tiered pricing).

Attachment: MSA_marketing_exception_snippet.txt (TXT)

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir@innovex.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Cc: Innovex Legal <legal@innovex.com>, press@innovex.com
Date: 2028-07-02T09:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Confidentiality and Marketing Asset Release — NDA Exception Request

Thanks Sofia / Kim — this looks reasonable. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Innovex marketing would prefer a 72-hour approval SLA rather than 3 business days (same intent but more consistent for international teams) — is that acceptable?
- For press releases: we often have embargoed briefings with partners and reporters. We need explicit language allowing embargoed press coordination and the ability to distribute embargoed drafts to press if the partner signs an embargo acknowledgement.
- Social posts: Would a micro-quote (one sentence) used in social channels (Twitter/LinkedIn) be covered by the same approval flow?

If you can tweak the snippet to say "72 hours" and explicitly allow embargoed-distribution to press with an embargo acknowledgement, we can sign off quickly. I'll loop in our Legal (legal@innovex.com) to confirm the language.

Samir Patel
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Innovex Systems
